report:
## Conclusion

The claim is well supported: the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, brand name Shingrix) substantially reduces the risk of herpes zoster (shingles) in adults aged 70 and older.

**Randomized trial evidence:** The pivotal ZOE-70 trial (NCT01165229), a randomized, placebo-controlled, observer-blind phase 3 study of nearly 14,000 adults ≥70 years, found RZV was about 91% efficacious against shingles in this age group over roughly 3.7 years of follow-up (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800). This mirrored the ~97% efficacy seen in the companion ZOE-50 trial covering ages 50+ (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184), showing efficacy remains robust even in the oldest, most immunosenescent participants.

**Durability:** An 11-year long-term follow-up extension of ZOE-50/ZOE-70 participants (reported by GSK and reflected in the EMA product information) shows protection persists for over a decade, with only gradual waning, supporting sustained benefit in older adults (https://us.gsk.com/en-us/media/press-releases/new-long-term-data-show-shingrix-continues-to-provide-high-protection-against-shingles/).

**Regulatory/public health endorsement:** Based on this trial evidence, the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices recommends two doses of RZV for all immunocompetent adults ≥50, explicitly including those over 70 (https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html).

**Caveats:** Efficacy is slightly lower in the ≥70 group (91%) than in 50–69 year-olds (97%), consistent with age-related immune decline, and long-term data, while reassuring, come mostly from an open-label extension rather than a placebo-controlled trial, introducing some risk of bias. Nonetheless, the totality of randomized and observational evidence strongly supports the claim.
